Head_and_Face: Distinct anterior head region bears eyespots (ocelli) and chemoreceptive auricles.
Free-living species display triangular or arrow-shaped head.
Parasitic forms are elongated and segmented without distinct head.
Body_and_Plumage: Dorsoventrally flattened leaf-like or ribbon-like body shape.
Surface texture is smooth, moist, and ciliated.
Color ranges from translucent white to brown, grey, or black.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Body is unsegmented with simple digestive system featuring single opening.
Locomotion via ciliary gliding or muscular undulations creating rippling motion.
No body cavity (acoelomate) present.

Head_and_Face: Head region bears sensory amphids and labial papillae.
Mouth opening may feature stylet in plant-parasitic species.
Head tapers to fine point at anterior end.
Body_and_Plumage: Elongated cylindrical body tapering to fine points at both ends.
Smooth flexible cuticle covering appearing translucent white, cream, or pale yellow.
Cross-section reveals round (not flattened) body plan.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Body is microscopic to very small, visible only under magnification or as tiny thread-like forms.
Locomotion via characteristic thrashing or sinusoidal undulations.
Body cavity is pseudocoelomate with longitudinal muscles only.

Head_and_Face: Paired eyestalks extend from soft body.
Siphon for water intake extends from aperture.
Head bears sensory tentacles.
Body_and_Plumage: Large spiral shell of substantial gastropod proportions with dextral coiling.
Shell displays flared outer lip often orange, pink, or brown with spiral ridges.
Shell surface is glossy calcareous with spiral growth lines.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Large muscular foot extends from aperture for locomotion.
Operculum is claw-shaped and corneous.
Shell interior exhibits pearlescent pink to white coloration.

Head_and_Face: Head bears two pairs of tentacles: upper pair with eyes at tips, lower pair for olfaction.
Tentacles are retractable and extend from shell aperture.
Eyes are positioned at tips of upper tentacle pair.
Body_and_Plumage: External spiral shell coiled in helical pattern, varying from minute to very large across species.
Shell exhibits dextral or sinistral coiling with brown, tan, yellow, or banded coloration.
Shell surface texture ranges from smooth and glossy to ribbed or granulated.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Broad muscular foot extends from shell for gliding locomotion.
Foot leaves characteristic mucous trail.
Mantle secretes shell material.

Head_and_Face: Head bears two pairs of retractable tentacles with eyes at tips of upper pair.
Tentacles are prominent and extend from anterior body.
Eyes are positioned at tips of upper tentacle pair.
Body_and_Plumage: Elongated soft body lacking external shell, of modest to moderate length.
Body surface is smooth, moist, and covered with protective mucus layer.
Coloration ranges from grey, brown, black, yellow, to orange with darker stripes or mottling.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Muscular foot extends entire ventral length for gliding locomotion.
Dorsal mantle visible as saddle-shaped structure on anterior third of body.
Leaves characteristic silvery mucous trail.

Head_and_Face: Head bears oral tentacles and rhinophores (sensory structures).
Rhinophores are feathery or club-shaped.
Oral tentacles extend from anterior body.
Body_and_Plumage: Shell-less body exhibiting vibrant coloration, varying from very small to moderately elongated.
Body displays brilliant hues of blue, purple, orange, yellow, green, or red with contrasting patterns.
Texture is smooth, gelatinous, and delicate.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Dorsal surface features prominent cerata (finger-like projections) or flattened notal plates.
Cerata are translucent to opaque often tipped with contrasting colors.
Locomotion via muscular foot or swimming undulations.

Head_and_Face: Head is reduced without eyes or tentacles.
Anterior end is blunt and indistinct.
No prominent sensory structures visible.
Body_and_Plumage: Dorsal surface protected by eight overlapping calcareous plates arranged in linear series.
Plates embedded in tough leathery girdle that may be smooth, spiny, or hairy.
Plate coloration ranges from grey, brown, green to mottled patterns.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Ventral surface features broad muscular foot for adhesion to rocky substrates.
Body exhibits dorsoventrally flattened profile when clinging to surfaces.
Can curl into defensive ball when dislodged.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are simple pits without lenses.
Numerous retractable tentacles arranged in two circles around mouth.
Tentacles lack suckers distinguishing from other cephalopods.
Body_and_Plumage: External spiral shell of moderate cephalopod proportions with planispiral coiling in single plane.
Outer shell surface is smooth, glossy, and white with radial brown or reddish-brown stripes.
Shell interior displays iridescent nacreous (mother-of-pearl) finish.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Funnel (hyponome) used for jet propulsion extends from shell aperture.
Shell contains numerous internal chambers separated by pale pearly septa.
Shell provides buoyancy control through gas-filled chambers.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are stalked and protrude from anterior carapace margin.
Carapace is smooth and convex displaying purplish-brown to reddish-brown coloration.
Ventral surface is cream to white.
Body_and_Plumage: Broad oval carapace of substantial edible-crab proportions.
Carapace displays lighter mottled patterns over purplish-brown base.
Exoskeleton is hard and calcified with smooth glossy texture.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Five pairs of walking legs extend laterally.
First pair modified into robust claws of unequal size with dark tips.
Claws have smooth outer surface and serrated inner edges.

Head_and_Face: Eyes are stalked and positioned at anterior carapace corners.
Carapace exhibits smooth convex surface with purple-brown to reddish-brown coloration.
Darker mottling and lighter margins visible on carapace.
Body_and_Plumage: Broad rounded carapace of modest size, noticeably smaller than Dungeness crab.
Ventral surface is pale cream to yellowish.
Exoskeleton is hard, calcified, and glossy.
Limbs_and_Anatomy: Five pairs of walking legs are relatively short and robust.
Claws are stout and unequal in size with dark brown to black tips.
Abdomen is folded ventrally with segmented structure visible in juveniles.
